registry_title: ShelterAI Thermal Vulnerability Data Source Provenance Registry
disclaimer: All datasets are compiled from published meteorological, governmental, and peer-reviewed Indian energy studies. They serve decision-support screening and do not represent formal governmental risk rankings.

sources.primary_source: India Meteorological Department (IMD) - Climatological Normals & Gridded Temperature Data
sources.units: Composite index derived from mean summer Tmax (°C) & annual Cooling Degree Days (CDD18)
sources.methodology: Min-max normalization of 30-year state-averaged maximum dry-bulb temperatures across peak summer months (March-June).
sources.limitations: Microclimatic topography variations within mountainous or coastal state pockets may experience local deviations.

sources.primary_source: IMD Extreme Weather Events Report & NDMA National Heat Action Plans
sources.spatial_resolution: District-level reports aggregated to State level
sources.units: Days/year with Tmax departure > 4.5°C over normal
sources.methodology: Normalized metric of annual cumulative heatwave days and severe heatwave declarations per state.
sources.limitations: Under-reporting of localized micro-heatwave pockets in non-monitored rural stations.

sources.primary_source: IMD & ERA5 Reanalysis Calibrated Data / National Institute of Occupational Health (NIOH)
sources.units: NOAA Heat Index & Simplified Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (sWBGT) exceedance hours
sources.methodology: Hourly calculation of wet-bulb temperature exceeding 28°C and Heat Index > 41°C during pre-monsoon and monsoon seasons.
sources.limitations: Indoor temperature elevations are modeled assuming standard naturally ventilated residential envelopes.

sources.primary_source: Bureau of Energy Efficiency (BEE) - India Energy Outlook & National Smart Grid Mission
sources.units: kWh/household/summer month & grid peak load ramp factor
sources.methodology: Calculated from baseline Cooling Degree Hours (base 24°C) combined with DISCOM peak seasonal surge reports.
sources.limitations: Informal cooling strategies (evaporative coolers, natural ventilation) are estimated via typical household saturation surveys.

sources.primary_source: Census of India & Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW) - NFHS-5 Survey
sources.units: % Elderly (>65), % Under-5 children, % Outdoor manual labor workforce
sources.methodology: Multi-attribute weighted sum of vulnerable age demographics, manual agrarian/construction employment, and baseline healthcare density.
sources.limitations: Decadal population growth projections applied between decennial census intervals.

sources.variable_name: Uninsulated & Kutcha Housing Stock Exposure Score (0-100)
sources.primary_source: Census Housing Tables & Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) - PMAY-U / PMAY-G Datasets
sources.units: % Shelters with uninsulated CGI sheet or tin roofs, % Kutcha wall structures
sources.methodology: Composite index of high-absorptance low-inertia roof materials (corrugated sheet, asbestos, uninsulated concrete slabs) lacking thermal barrier treatment.
sources.limitations: Incremental vernacular roof retrofits (thatch over sheet) may not be fully captured in formal housing records.

sources.primary_source: NITI Aayog SDG India Index & Central Electricity Authority (CEA) Power Supply Reports
sources.units: Composite index of 24x7 grid reliability, primary healthcare access, forest canopy cover, and state Heat Action Plan (HAP) implementation status
sources.methodology: Normalized score measuring preparedness, institutional heat response protocols, municipal cool roof mandates, and green cover buffer.
sources.limitations: Inter-district disparity inside large states (e.g. Western vs Eastern Maharashtra) is aggregated into state-level averages.
